Former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has vowed to restore fuel and electricity subsidies if elected president in the 2027 general election. Atiku made the pledge on Sunday during a political rally at Dabo Aliyu Stadium in Potiskum Local Government Area of Yobe State, where thousands of supporters gathered to receive him. The former Vice-President said his administration would reverse the removal of petrol and electricity subsidies, arguing that the measures would provide relief to Nigerians grappling with rising living costs. Addressing the crowd, Atiku said, “Let me assure you that once I am elected president in 2027, I will bring back the fuel subsidy. As I have said in other places, let me reiterate that I swear I will bring back the fuel subsidy once I am elected president. “I swear I will also bring back the subsidy on electricity.” He also pledged to tackle insecurity in Yobe State and other parts of the country, promising that his administration would take decisive measures to restore peace and prevent criminal elements from operating freely. “Let me assure you that I will ensure that peace returns to Yobe State and the country at large. Criminal elements will have no haven once I am elected president,” he said. On youth unemployment, Atiku promised to create job opportunities for young Nigerians, saying his administration would prioritise employment and economic empowerment. He expressed concern over the number of unemployed youths in the country, insisting that deliberate policies would be introduced to improve their livelihoods. “Let me assure you that I will ensure that our youths are fully employed in Nigeria. We will not have jobless youths once I am elected,” the ADC presidential candidate said. Atiku urged Nigerians to support the ADC in the 2027 general election, describing the party as a platform through which the country could address its economic and security challenges. “ADC will bring a better life to you. We are here to shape your future,” he told the supporters.
